newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - Victoria moves closer to AAA.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - Victoria moves closer to AAA.

text.p: *Victorian state debt moved closer to achieving triple-A status after last week's Budget.
*New South Wales budget due on Tuesday.
The Australian state of Victoria moved a step nearer to AAA status following last week's budget, although its debt has been trading in this guise for some time.

Victorian Treasurer Alan Stockdale forecast an underlying budget surplus of A$443.7 million for 1997/98 and revised the underlying outcome for 1996/97 to a surplus of A$802.7 million from its projected 700,000 deficit.
U.S. rating agency Standard & Poor's Inc said last week that while the state has moved closer to an upgrade, it would want to see that the budget surpluses are entrenched.

However, "(Victorian) debt is now at level comparable to other states with AAA ratings, so combined with improved state of the budget balance over recent years, a Victorian upgrade cannot be too far away," said David Thurtell, analyst at Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
"This, and the 1997/98 budget, should assist in keeping downward pressure on Victorian spreads," he added.
Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV), the state's treasury arm, projected an indicative funding programme of A$1.5 billion for 1997/98, which will consist entirely of refinancing maturities.
TCV expects the net call on the market to be A$800 million in the fiscal year and it expects to maintain regular bond tenders every six to eight weeks.
This Tuesday sees the New South Wales budget, the last of state budgets before the Federal Budget on May 13 with Queensland due on May 27 and South Australia due on May 29.
Meanwhile, Western Australia Treasury Corp issued a two-year 40 billion yen dual currency (Australian dollar/yen) samurai bond last week through Nomura Securities.
